blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: object — An instance of a class
field — Data associated with an object

blocks.title: Class ≠ instance
blocks.text: A class defines the fields and behaviour available to each object. new Student() constructs an instance; a separate new creates another independent object.

blocks.title: Worked example · One class, two independent objects
blocks.text: using System; Badge amber = new Badge(); Badge blue = new Badge(); amber.Add(2); Console.WriteLine(amber.Points + "," + blue.Points); class Badge { public int Points = 0; public void Add(int n) { Points += n; } }

blocks.title: Worked example · Identify class, objects and members
blocks.text: Badge is the class (blueprint). amber and blue are references to two objects. Each has its own Points field and can run the Add method.

blocks.title: Worked example · Trace the state change
blocks.text: new Badge() creates each object with Points = 0. amber.Add(2) changes amber’s field from 0 to 2; blue remains at 0 because it is a different instance.

questions.feedback: object — An instance of a class
field — Data associated with an object

blocks.title: Different class, different data
blocks.text: using System; Counter first = new Counter(); Counter second = new Counter(); first.Increase(); first.Increase(); Console.WriteLine(first.Value + "," + second.Value); class Counter { public int Value = 0; public void Increase() { Value++; } } What are first.Value and second.Value?

blocks.title: Trace both instances
blocks.text: Start with separate fields: first = 0, second = 0. Track which object receives each method call before revealing the result.

blocks.title: Independent state
blocks.text: first.Value = 2 and second.Value = 0. Both calls act on first; they do not change second.

blocks.title: Change the receiver
blocks.text: Continue from Example 1: second.Increase(); What values are stored now? Explain what second identifies.
